extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners, and third parties considering or litigating Post Grant Review (PGR) proceedings before the PTAB
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for initiating and defending Post Grant Review (PGR) trials before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), including filing deadlines, institution standards, timing for final decisions, and applicability under the AIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Post grant review is a trial proceeding conducted at the Board to review the patentability of one or more claims in a patent on any ground that could be raised under § 282(b)(2) or (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines PGR as an adversarial trial before the PTAB specifically focused on claim patentability (distinct from other trials like inter partes review or derivation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file the petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Post grant review process begins with a third party filing a petition...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a third party (i.e., someone other than the patent owner) may initiate a PGR by filing the petition with the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing time limit (statutory window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition must be filed on or prior to the date that is 9 months after the grant of the patent or issuance of a reissue patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 9‑month deadline is jurisdictional for standard PGRs; petitions filed after this window will not be proper PGRs (other remedies may apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Available grounds for challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Review may be on any ground that could be raised under § 282(b)(2) or (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR is broader in allowed grounds than some other post‑grant proceedings because it permits any ground available under those subsections (consult § 282(b)(2)/(3) for specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary response by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a preliminary response to the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a preliminary response is optional but serves as the patent owner's initial substantive defense to persuade the Board not to institute review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard (threshold for initiating trial)
rubrics_metrics.description: A post grant review may be instituted upon a showing that, it is more likely than not that at least one claim challenged is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTAB applies the 'more likely than not' (preponderance of evidence) standard at institution — petitioners must show a greater than 50% likelihood that at least one challenged claim is unpatentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for final determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proceeding is instituted and not dismissed, a final determination by the Board will be issued within 1 year (extendable for good cause by 6 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board aims to complete PGRs within 12 months from institution, but may extend up to an additional 6 months for good cause; parties should plan discovery and briefing schedules accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability under the AIA / effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for conducting post grant review took effect on September 16, 2012, and generally applies to patents issuing from applications subject to first-inventor-to-file provisions of the AIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR procedures primarily govern post‑grant reviews of patents that arise from AIA first‑inventor‑to‑file applications; check whether a particular patent falls within that scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative rules and guidance to consult
rubrics_metrics.description: References: General Administrative Trial Final Rules (77 Fed. Reg. 48612, August 14, 2012); Trial Practice Guide (77 Fed. Reg. 48756, August 14, 2012); Inter Partes, Post Grant, and Covered Business Method Review Final Rules (77 Fed. Reg. 48680, August 14, 2012); Proposed Rule of Practice for Trials before the PTAB (77 Fed. Reg. 6879, Feb. 9, 2012); Proposed Trial Practice Guide (77 Fed. Reg. 6868, Feb. 9, 2012); Proposed Rules for Post Grant Review (77 Fed. Reg. 7060, February 10, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should consult these Federal Register notices and the PTAB Trial Practice Guide for full procedural and practice details governing PGR petitions, institution decisions, evidence, motions, and trial conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching existing PGRs (P‑TACTS)
rubrics_metrics.description: To search for an PGR, click on the system link for P-TACTS. Additional information is located on the P-TACTS information page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the P-TACTS system to find existing PGR filings and dockets, which can inform strategy and provide procedural examples.
